question: What minimum vertical clearance is required for overhead signs over the pavement and shoulders?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Overhead signs must provide a vertical clearance of not less than 17 feet, measured to the sign, light fixture, or sign bridge, over the entire width of the pavement and shoulders. A lesser clearance is permitted only where the mounting structure or other nearby structures along the roadway have a lesser vertical clearance, and in special cases such as tunnels or double-deck bridges. The 17-foot minimum is echoed in the preferential-lane provisions for signs post-mounted on median barriers. Standards (mandatory): - "Overhead signs shall provide a vertical clearance of not less than 17 feet to the sign, light fixture, or sign bridge over the entire width of the pavement and shoulders, except where the structure on which the overhead signs are to be mounted or other structures along the roadway near the sign structure have a lesser vertical clearance." (Section 2A.15, visible in [Image 2]) - "Signs that are post-mounted on a median barrier that overhang any portion of the traveled way shall be mounted with a vertical clearance that complies with that of overhead signs." (Section 2A.15, visible in [Image 2]) Options (permitted): - "If the vertical clearance of other structures along the roadway near the sign structure is less than 16 feet, the vertical clearance to an overhead sign structure or support may be as low as 1 foot higher than the vertical clearance of the other structures in order to improve the visibility of the overhead signs." (Section 2A.15, visible in [Image 2]) - "In special cases the clearance to overhead signs may be reduced if necessary because of substandard dimensions in tunnels and other major structures such as double-deck bridges." (Section 2A.15, visible in [Image 2]) - Where lateral clearance is limited, Preferential Lane regulatory signs post-mounted on a median barrier that are 72 inches or less in width may be skewed up to 45 degrees or mounted higher, "such that the vertical clearance to the bottom of the sign, light fixture, or structural support, whichever is lowest, is not less than 17 feet above any portion of the pavement and shoulders." - The same 17-foot vertical clearance allowance applies to barrier-mounted warning signs applicable only to a preferential lane and to Preferential Lane guide signs 72 inches or less in width. Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 2A-2, panel "H – Overhead sign," illustrates the 17 ft MIN vertical clearance from the pavement/shoulder to the bottom of an overhead sign (along with the 6 ft MIN lateral offset for the support). - [Image 2] shows the Section 2A.15 Standard text requiring not less than 17 feet of vertical clearance to the sign, light fixture, or sign bridge over the entire width of the pavement and shoulders, plus the related Options for reduced clearance near lower structures. Citations: - Figure 2A-2 (p.51) - Page 100 - Section 2G.03 Option §14 (p.411) - Section 2G.08 Option §4 (p.419) - Section 2G.10 Option §18 (p.422)
gold_answer: At least 17 feet, except where nearby structures or special constrained structures qualify for the specific exceptions in Section 2A.15.
